initial.name: bash
initial.description:
Run commands in a bash shell
* When invoking this tool, the contents of the "command" parameter does NOT need to be XML-escaped.
* You don't have access to the internet via this tool.
* You do have access to a mirror of common linux and python packages via apt and pip.
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user.
* To inspect a particular line range of a file, e.g. lines 10-25, try 'sed -n 10,25p /path/to/the/file'.
* Please avoid commands that may produce a very large amount of output.
* Please run long lived commands in the background, e.g. 'sleep 10 &' or start a server in the background.

command.description: The bash command to run. Relative path is preferred in the command.

initial.name: mesh_agents
initial.description: List the external coding agents the mesh can read (Codex, Grok Build, Pi, OMP), with their detection state and declared capabilities.

initial.name: mesh_collaboration_start
initial.description: Create a collaboration: one authoritative plan, one shared todo board, and optional tasks assigned to agents. A worktree-isolated task gets its own git worktree when it is dispatched.

objective.description: What the collaboration as a whole must achieve.

repoRoot.description: Absolute path of the repository the tasks work in.

tasks.description: Initial tasks. A seed may name a sibling by position ("task-1") or by id in dependsOn.

initial.name: mesh_collaborations
initial.description: List collaborations with their plan, board counts, tasks and worktrees, or read one collaboration by id.

collaborationId.description: Read one collaboration instead of listing every one.

initial.name: mesh_plan_advance
initial.description: Move the plan to a phase, marking every earlier phase done. Refused while an earlier phase is still open.

initial.name: mesh_plan_set
initial.description: Replace a collaboration's plan fields. The plan is the authoritative input every dispatched run receives.

objective.description: The objective; it replaces the current one.

phases.description: The complete new phase list, in order.

activePhaseId.description: Phase to mark active; it must exist in the resulting list.

mode.description: Whether the plan is injected into dispatched prompts or only observed.

initial.name: mesh_run
initial.description: Dispatch a task to an external coding agent's own CLI in a working directory. The run continues after this call returns; read it with mesh_runs.

agentId.description: Agent id, as reported by mesh_agents.

prompt.description: The task to hand the agent.

cwd.description: Absolute working directory the agent runs in.

model.description: Model in the agent's own naming.

approval.description: Approval mode in the agent's own vocabulary.

initial.name: mesh_run_cancel
initial.description: Cancel a dispatched run. Cancellation terminates the agent process group; it is not a resumable pause.

initial.name: mesh_runs
initial.description: Read dispatched runs: their status, final answer, classified failure, and recent events.

runId.description: One run to read; omit for every tracked run.

wait.description: With runId, wait for that run to reach a terminal status before answering.

initial.name: mesh_sessions
initial.description: List one external agent's own sessions (as that agent's CLI stored them), newest first.

agentId.description: Agent id, as reported by mesh_agents.

cwd.description: Only sessions whose recorded working directory resolves to this path.

limit.description: Maximum number of sessions to return.

initial.name: mesh_task_dispatch
initial.description: Dispatch one collaboration task: create or reuse its worktree, hand the agent the plan and board context plus the instruction, and record the run on the task. Refused when the task is already running or succeeded, or when a dependency is unfinished.

taskId.description: Task to dispatch, as reported by mesh_collaborations.

baseRef.description: Commit-ish a newly created worktree branches from.

timeoutMs.description: Wall-clock budget handed to the agent.

initial.name: mesh_tasks
initial.description: Read one external agent's own todo list and plan for a session, when that agent records them.

agentId.description: Agent id, as reported by mesh_agents.

sessionId.description: Native session id, as reported by mesh_sessions.

initial.name: mesh_todos_get
initial.description: Read a collaboration's shared todo board with its revision.

initial.name: mesh_todos_observe
initial.description: Read one agent's own todo list for a session and fold it into the shared board. Authored items are never overwritten, and an item the board considers done is never reopened.

collaborationId.description: Collaboration whose board is folded into.

agentId.description: Agent whose own store is read, as reported by mesh_agents.

sessionId.description: The agent's native session id; the newest session is read when omitted.

initial.name: mesh_todos_set
initial.description: Replace a collaboration's shared todo board. Pass expectedRevision from a previous read to be refused instead of clobbering another writer's change.

expectedRevision.description: Revision the caller read; the write is refused when the board moved on.

initial.name: mesh_transcript
initial.description: Read a window of one external agent's session transcript, projected onto a common message shape.

agentId.description: Agent id, as reported by mesh_agents.

sessionId.description: Native session id, as reported by mesh_sessions.

maxMessages.description: Maximum number of trailing messages to return.

initial.name: mesh_worktree_conflicts
initial.description: Compare the live worktrees of one repository and report the files two of them changed. Detection is advisory: it reports same-file overlap only, never a semantic conflict in different files.

initial.name: mesh_worktree_create
initial.description: Create a git worktree on a new branch inside the mesh-owned directory of a repository, or reuse a clean idle one already reserved for that agent.

agentId.description: Agent the worktree is reserved for.

baseRef.description: Commit-ish to branch from; the repository HEAD when omitted.

label.description: Label used in the branch name and the worktree directory.

reuse.description: Reuse a clean idle worktree reserved for the same agent.

initial.name: mesh_worktree_integrated
initial.description: Mark a worktree integrated so it stops appearing as outstanding work, or outstanding again with merged=false.

merged.description: false marks it outstanding again; defaults to true.

initial.name: mesh_worktree_remove
initial.description: Remove a mesh-owned git worktree. DANGEROUS: a worktree with uncommitted changes or unmerged commits is refused unless force is true, and a forced removal discards that work permanently.

force.description: Discard uncommitted and unmerged work. Only pass this after a human approved the loss.

initial.name: mesh_worktrees
initial.description: List mesh-owned git worktrees with a live progress sample: changed files, HEAD, and whether the tree is dirty.

repoRoot.description: Restrict to worktrees of one repository.

initial.name: str_replace_editor
initial.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* A null placeholder for a parameter unused by the selected command is treated as omitted. Required parameters still need values; omit `str_replace.new_str` rather than setting it to null when deleting a match

Notes for using the `str_replace` command:
* The `old_str` parameter should match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the original file. Be mindful of whitespaces!
* If the `old_str` parameter is not unique in the file, the replacement will not be performed. Make sure to include enough context in `old_str` to make it unique
* The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that should replace the `old_str`

command.description: The commands to run. Allowed options are: `view`, `create`, `str_replace`, `insert`.

path.description: Absolute path to file or directory, e.g. `/repo/file.py` or `/repo`.

file_text.description: Required string parameter of `create` command, with the content of the file to be created. A null placeholder is treated as omitted by commands that do not use this parameter.

insert_line.description: Required integer parameter of `insert` command. The `new_str` will be inserted AFTER the line `insert_line` of `path`. A null placeholder is treated as omitted by commands that do not use this parameter.

new_str.description: Optional string parameter of `str_replace` command containing the new string (if omitted, no string will be added). Required string parameter of `insert` command containing the string to insert. A null placeholder is accepted only by commands that do not use this parameter.

old_str.description: Required string parameter of `str_replace` command containing the string in `path` to replace. A null placeholder is treated as omitted by commands that do not use this parameter.

view_range.description: Optional parameter of `view` command when `path` points to a file. If omitted or null, the full file is shown. If provided, the file will be shown in the indicated line number range, e.g. [11, 12] will show lines 11 and 12. Indexing at 1 to start. Setting `[start_line, -1]` shows all lines from `start_line` to the end of the file.

initial.name: working_directory
initial.description: Read the current working directory, or change it with cd. Relative paths use the current directory. Existing shells and running processes keep their own directories.

cd.description: Existing directory to enter. Omit to read the current directory.
